xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-3331: feat(dashboard): workspace quick-action band — git sync card, run command, open-in-external — above the memory feed

plan.title: feat(dashboard): workspace quick-action band — git sync card, run command, open-in-external — above the memory feed
plan.author: agent:claude-fable-5

narratives.Problem: WorkspaceView jumps from its title bar straight into the terminal/conversations/memory panels and answers none of the three most common operational questions: is my checkout current with its remote (ahead/behind exists only in the issue-workspace route and compares HEAD...origin/HEAD instead of the branch's own upstream, and nothing ever fetches), how do I run this thing (POST /api/terminals discards its command argument), and how do I open it in other tools (no reveal/editor affordance exists). Stale checkouts caused three separate failures on 2026-07-29.
narratives.Proposal: Insert a full-width quick-action band between WorkspaceView's header and its panel group, for all workspace kinds: (1) a git sync card backed by a new upstream-correct git-state module with rate-limited real fetch and a guarded fast-forward-only Pull (issue kinds delegate to the existing sync-main flow); (2) a run card that launches the per-workspace run command (defaulting from services[].start_command, persisted in a new run_command column) into a tmux session whose terminal attaches in-view; (3) an open-in menu (reveal in file manager always, open-in-editor gated on new ui.open_in_editor_command config). All registry access through the two doors; all spawns async argument vectors.
narratives.NonGoals:
- A 'flagged' workspace marker (favorites already serve the role)
- Push/publish actions or merge/rebase from the band (Pull is ff-only; everything else stays in existing flows)
- Global keyboard shortcut registry (palette action only)
- Scheduled background fetching for workspaces not on screen (cadence is view-scoped by D-8)
- Any change to issue-workspace sync-main semantics
- Any change to existing routes, panels, or layout persistence (no-loss, NFR-4)

autoDecisions.summary: Adopted the canonical PRD on overdeck-state (drafts/pan-3331.md) as authoritative without operator questions.
autoDecisions.rationale: The PRD is complete (glossary, 10 verified-state claims, D-1..D-10, FR-1..9/NFR-1..6, work items with named tests, 1:1 ACs, non-goals) and every file/line anchor re-verified against the workspace base main@078f1f1a72.

autoDecisions.summary: The run route validates the resolved command (400 on newline, backtick, or >500 chars) before spawning.
autoDecisions.rationale: Async createSession (src/lib/tmux.ts:1053) passes initialCommand through unvalidated, unlike the deprecated sync variant which special-cases those inputs via a temp script; rejecting at the route is the smallest safe behavior and avoids porting temp-script complexity into the async path.

autoDecisions.summary: ui.open_in_editor_command lands as a net-new optional `ui` section in src/lib/config-yaml/schema.ts with a getOpenInEditorCommand() accessor in src/lib/config.ts.
autoDecisions.rationale: No `ui` yaml section exists today and the existing 'UI theme' is a separate file (~/.overdeck/ui-theme.json, src/lib/ui-theme.ts) that must not be overloaded; the accessor follows the existing getConversationsConfigSync + Effect-variant pattern in config.ts.

autoDecisions.summary: openPath follows openBrowser's Effect-based shape (Effect.Effect<void, ProcessSpawnError, ChildProcessSpawner>).
autoDecisions.rationale: openBrowser at src/lib/browser.ts:26 is Effect-based; a sibling helper with the same signature keeps the module consistent and testable with the same spawner mocks.

autoDecisions.summary: Only the git-state module item carries requiresInspection: true.
autoDecisions.rationale: Its exported types and typed refusal reasons are the contract that the routes item and the band UI item both encode; every other item is a leaf whose defects surface at typecheck, tests, or review.

items.title: git-state module: upstream-correct state + ff-only pull with typed refusals

expected_outputs: tests/unit/lib/workspaces/git-state.test.ts passes with temp-repo fixtures covering ahead/behind, fallback, detached, and every typed pull refusal
metadata.readinessReason: Creates only new files (git-state.ts and its test); its single shared file (types.ts) gets an additive type export, and after serialization no other item runs in the same wave.

narrative.Action: Create src/lib/workspaces/git-state.ts exporting getWorkspaceGitState(path, {fetch?: boolean}): Promise<WorkspaceGitState> and pullWorkspaceFastForward(path), with the WorkspaceGitState type ({branch, detached, dirtyFiles, ahead, behind, hasUpstream, upstreamRef, recentRemoteCommits: [{sha, subject, author, date}], fetchedAt}) added in src/lib/workspaces/types.ts. Ahead/behind via `git rev-list --left-right --count HEAD...@{u}`, falling back to origin/HEAD with hasUpstream:false when no upstream is set; recent remote commits via `git log HEAD..@{u} --format=... -n 10`. pullWorkspaceFastForward executes `git pull --ff-only <remote> <branch>` and returns (never throws) typed refusal reasons: 'dirty' (git status --porcelain non-empty), 'operation-in-progress' (reuse ensureSyncGitQuiescent from src/lib/cloister/sync-main-git.ts:139), 'not-fast-forward', 'no-upstream', 'detached'. All git invocations use execFileAsync argument vectors (no shell strings, no execSync). Tests use temp-repo fixtures (real git repos in tmp dirs), per PRD WI-1.

items.title: Given a feature branch behind its own upstream but even with origin/HEAD, getWorkspaceGitState returns the upstream's ahead/behind counts (not origin/HEAD's) with hasUpstream:true and the upstreamRef named
Given a branch with no upstream, getWorkspaceGitState falls back to origin/HEAD for counts and returns hasUpstream:false; given a detached HEAD it returns detached:true
pullWorkspaceFastForward returns typed refusal values (not thrown strings) for each of: dirty tree, in-flight git operation, non-fast-forwardable divergence, no upstream, detached HEAD
Given a clean behind-only checkout, pullWorkspaceFastForward advances the branch to its upstream and a subsequent getWorkspaceGitState returns behind:0
recentRemoteCommits returns {sha, subject, author, date} entries capped at 10, and every git invocation in the module spawns via execFileAsync argument vectors (no shell-interpolated strings)
GET git-state + POST pull routes on workspace-registry with rate-limited fetch

narrative.Action: In src/dashboard/server/routes/workspace-registry.ts add GET /api/workspace-registry/:id/git?fetch=0|1 and POST /api/workspace-registry/:id/pull, following the file's existing guard/readJsonBody patterns (:83-92, :159-161). GET resolves the workspace via the resolver, returns 404 for unknown ids, returns {git: null} with 200 for isGitRepository=false rows, otherwise returns WorkspaceGitState from the git-state module. fetch=1 triggers `git fetch <remote> <branch>` first, rate-limited by an in-memory per-path last-fetch map: fetches within 30s of the previous are skipped while state is still recomputed. POST pull is mutation-guarded (rejectUnsafeDashboardMutationRequest), returns 409 for kind='issue' directing to sync-main, otherwise runs pullWorkspaceFastForward and returns the new state or the typed refusal verbatim. Rate-limit tests use vi.useFakeTimers() + advanceTimersByTimeAsync — never real waits.

items.title: GET with fetch=1 fetches then returns fresh state; a second fetch=1 within 30s skips the fetch but still returns recomputed state (proven with fake timers advancing past the window)
GET returns 404 for an unknown workspace id and 200 {git: null} for a row with isGitRepository=false
POST pull rejects unguarded/unsafe requests via rejectUnsafeDashboardMutationRequest and returns 409 for kind='issue' workspaces
POST pull passes typed refusal reasons from pullWorkspaceFastForward through to the response body unchanged, and returns the refreshed WorkspaceGitState on success
run_command column, writer/resolver support, and run-command + run routes

expected_outputs: tests/unit/dashboard/workspace-run.test.ts passes including single-live-session and default-resolution cases

narrative.Action: Add nullable `run_command` text column to the workspaces table in ensureWorkspaceTablesSync (src/lib/overdeck/infra.ts:230 area — the idempotent top-up; NEVER store it in layout_config, which react-resizable-panels round-trips and clobbers). Add setWorkspaceRunCommand(id, command: string | null) in src/lib/workspaces/writer.ts beside updateWorkspaceLayout (:122); surface runCommand on WorkspaceRow via resolver.ts/types.ts. Add PUT /api/workspace-registry/:id/run-command (guarded) to set/clear it, and POST /api/workspace-registry/:id/run (guarded) that resolves runCommand ?? first services[].start_command from project config (src/lib/workspace-config.ts:75-81), validates the command (400 on newline, backtick, or >500 chars — async createSession has no initialCommand validation), spawns createSession('ws-run-<8charid>', workspace.path, command, {env}) from src/lib/tmux.ts:1053 (async Effect variant only), and returns {sessionName, command}. Enforce one live run session per workspace: when one is alive, respond 409 {sessionName} with a distinct code so the UI re-focuses instead of duplicating. Stop uses the existing DELETE /api/terminals/:name.

items.title: PUT run-command persists an override through setWorkspaceRunCommand and the resolver returns it on subsequent reads; PUT with null clears it back to default resolution
POST run with no stored override resolves the command from the project's first services[].start_command and spawns createSession with (sessionName, workspace.path, exact command)
POST run while a run session is alive returns 409 with the live sessionName and spawns nothing (single-live-session semantics)
POST run rejects commands containing a newline or backtick or exceeding 500 characters with 400 before any tmux spawn
All registry reads/writes go through resolver.ts/writer.ts and the new column lands only in ensureWorkspaceTablesSync — scripts/guard-workspace-doors.sh exits green
openPath helper, ui.open_in_editor_command config, and open route

narrative.Action: Add openPath(path) beside openBrowser in src/lib/browser.ts with the same Effect-based shape (Effect.Effect<void, ProcessSpawnError, ChildProcessSpawner>) and platform branching (darwin `open`, linux `xdg-open` with fallback, win32 `explorer`). Add a net-new optional `ui` section to the config-yaml schema (src/lib/config-yaml/schema.ts): ui?: { open_in_editor_command?: string } — no `ui` yaml section exists today, and ~/.overdeck/ui-theme.json (src/lib/ui-theme.ts) is a separate file that must NOT be overloaded. Add a getOpenInEditorCommand() accessor in src/lib/config.ts following the getConversationsConfigSync/Effect-variant pattern (:496+). Add POST /api/workspace-registry/:id/open with body {target: 'file-manager' | 'editor'}, mutation-guarded (it spawns processes): file-manager always available via openPath; editor available only when ui.open_in_editor_command is set (409 when unset) — the template is split into tokens, {path} substituted per-token, and spawned as an argument vector, never a shell string.

items.title: POST open {target:'editor'} returns 409 when ui.open_in_editor_command is unset, and spawns the configured command with {path} substituted when set
Editor template execution spawns an argument vector with {path} substituted per token; a test rejects any code path that passes the template through a shell string
POST open {target:'file-manager'} spawns the platform file-manager opener via openPath (darwin open, linux xdg-open, win32 explorer) with the spawner mocked in tests
The open route rejects unguarded requests via rejectUnsafeDashboardMutationRequest and rejects unknown target values with 400
WorkspaceActionBand component wired into WorkspaceView for all kinds

expected_outputs: WorkspaceActionBand.test.tsx passes covering all git-card states, run flow, open-in gating, and fake-timer poll cadence

narrative.Action: Create src/dashboard/frontend/src/components/workspace/WorkspaceActionBand.tsx and insert it in WorkspaceView.tsx immediately after the header bar (after :186, before the conditional issue-panels block), shrink-0, rendered for every workspace kind. Git card: branch (mono), dirty-file count, ahead/behind vs upstream, expandable recent-remote-commits list, manual refresh affordance, and a Pull action that calls POST /api/workspace-registry/:id/pull for main/scratch kinds but POST /api/issues/:issueId/sync-main for issue kind (the UI never calls pull for issue kind). Data via one useQuery ['workspace-registry', id, 'git'] with refetchInterval 30000, staleTime 25000, initial request fetch=1. Honest degradations: non-git hides the card; detached HEAD shows a warning chip instead of Pull; no-upstream labels the fallback comparison. Run card: command display with edit→PUT run-command, Run→POST run→mount <XTerminal sessionName> in the terminal panel area (for main/scratch the run session becomes the panel content replacing 'No active agent terminal'; for issue kind it renders alongside), Stop→DELETE /api/terminals/:name, Restart=kill+spawn, 409 re-focuses the live session. Open-in menu: reveal always, editor entry only when config-gated endpoint reports availability. Style guide binds: mono for branch/sha/path, one colored signal per card (behind-count dot may use amber), Pull is the git card's single primary action. Implementer verifies rendering with Playwright screenshots at narrow + wide widths in an isolated browser instance — never asks the operator to eyeball.

items.title: The band renders after the header for issue, main, and scratch kinds; the git card renders clean/ahead/behind/dirty/detached/no-upstream states and stays hidden for non-git workspaces
Pull calls the kind-correct endpoint (sync-main for issue kind, registry pull otherwise) and the card re-renders the refreshed state; the expander lists recent remote commits

Run card edit persists via PUT run-command; Run POSTs and mounts XTerminal with the returned sessionName in the terminal panel area; Stop calls DELETE /api/terminals/:name; a 409 re-focuses the existing session
The git query polls at 30s with staleTime 25s and stops when the view unmounts (proven with fake timers); the open-in menu shows the editor entry only when the config gate reports it available

The change preserves existing panels, layout persistence, and the issue-panels block unchanged (no-loss), and Playwright screenshots at narrow and wide widths from an isolated browser session render the band per the style guide
Command palette 'Run workspace command' action

expected_outputs: palette suite passes asserting the action's presence in both scopes and its callback wiring

narrative.Action: Add a 'Run workspace command' action to CommandPalette.tsx via the staticActions pattern (:437-455), registered in both the workspaces and actions scopes, that triggers the run flow (POST /api/workspace-registry/:id/run) for the active workspace. No global keybinding — the dashboard has no keybinding registry and that is explicitly out of scope. Extend the existing palette test suite; if the palette suite lives under a different filename than CommandPalette.test.tsx, extend the file that already asserts staticActions entries.

items.title: The palette shows 'Run workspace command' in both the workspaces and actions scopes
Selecting the action sends POST /api/workspace-registry/:id/run for the active workspace (wiring asserted in the palette test suite)

CLAUDE.md, the pan-workspace skill, and docs/audits/pan-1990-surface-inventory.md reflect the band's surfaces, and npm run lint (including lint-skills) exits green

metadata.sizeJustification: 22 files is under the 25-file limit; the 8-subsystem count is an artifact of the mandated FR-9 documentation files each registering as a distinct subsystem under the first-two-segment heuristic (docs/WORKSPACES-AND-PROJECTS.md, docs/audits, configuration/workspaces.mdx, CLAUDE.md, sync-sources/skills). The code surface spans only three subsystems (src/lib, src/dashboard, tests/unit). The three band capabilities share one component, one route file, and one registry schema, and the doc files are required same-PR updates per the canonical PRD's FR-9 (PAN-3290 lesson) — splitting into sibling issues would ship a band with missing cards or docs that describe unshipped surfaces.
